description: Committee recommends enhancing 2025 civic survey demographic reporting.
Also, prepare 2026 budget option for more diverse community input.

chips.text: Recommended
Councillor Donauer cautioned against splitting the city into too many small groups.
Survey aims to better capture views from disabled, Indigenous, people of color

description: Increases Councillor communications allowance by $15,000 each.
Raises Councillor travel and training budgets by $37,400 total.
Future review of Councillor administrative support in 2027.

chips.text: Approved
Confidentiality concerns influenced increasing CCRA over direct administrative staff.
Councillor assistants may see reduced workload due to increased CCRA.
Future Councillor communications and travel budgets will be indexed to inflation annually.
Mayor's office resourcing was not addressed, but will be in a separate future report.

description: Committee recommends Council adopt a 1.71 non-residential to residential tax ratio.
The 1.71 ratio maintains 68% residential, 32% non-residential tax split.
New warehouse property assessments prompted the ratio change.

chips.text: Recommended to Council
Councillors debated making tax policy decisions before business community engagement.
Residential and non-residential property owners are directly affected.
Greater Saskatoon Chamber of Commerce submitted a letter regarding tax policy.
Administration is implementing additional reviews to prevent future assessment errors.

description: Committee recommends seeking $3.3M annually federal transit funding.
City must contribute $5M annually for 10 years.
Funds support buses, infrastructure, and active transportation.

chips.text: Recommended to Council
Councillor Donauer questioned EV bus cost and utility versus diesel buses.
Mayor Block questioned the risk of underfunding transit and impact on ridership.
Federal program requires transition to zero-emission buses by 2028-2029.
Administration will discuss adjusting zero-emission bus requirements with federal government.

description: City administration is developing 2026-2027 budget estimates.
Forecasts will go to Governance and Priorities Committee in Q2.

chips.text: Received as information

description: Council will review 2026/2027 budget forecasts in Q2.
Administration to present priority-based budgeting options in May.

chips.text: Councillor Donauer argued city cannot afford to be all things to all people.

description: City pauses private partner agreement for downtown arena.
Pause is for six months to assess economic conditions.
City not yet legally bound to the agreement.

chips.text: Mayor Block highlighted the enormous cost of not proceeding with the project.
Taxpayers face $300-500 million renovation cost if project stalls.
Public misunderstands project funding, believing it relies on property taxes.
Solicitor flagged potential legal implications if Council cancels procurement.
Administration promises to report back on agreement status within six months.

description: Saskatoon has 1,499 people experiencing homelessness.
A new 40-bed temporary shelter opened on Pacific Avenue.
City seeks site for new 60-bed permanent shelter.

chips.text: Approved
Mayor Block stated the city is not meeting resident expectations for supporting unhoused people.
175 youth are among the 1,499 people experiencing homelessness in Saskatoon.
Whether people are moving through shelters into housing, or if the same individuals remain
Over 80% of Saskatoon's homeless population is Indigenous.
Administration promised public information meetings once the permanent shelter site is finalized.

description: City will seek more staff for future elections.
Future reports propose election bylaw and legislative changes.
City may ask province to separate election dates.

chips.text: Councillor asks for data to support changing election dates from provincial.
School board budgets were not fully charged for city election staff.
Shared electronic voters list with province was a first-time process.
Staff committed to providing data-based information for provincial requests.

description: One mayoral candidate did not file campaign disclosures.
Two council candidates filed disclosures late.
City will prosecute non-compliant election candidates.

chips.text: Defeated
Councillor Pierce moved to evaluate election expense caps compared to other cities.
Why Saskatoon's election campaign spending caps are higher than other cities remains unclear.
Councillor Jeffries opposed reviewing caps, citing long-standing formula adjusted for inflation.

description: Public letters on the climate action plan were received.

chips.text: Climate organizer Joy-Vermetz spoke on climate action plan letters.

description: Integrity Commissioner received 14 formal complaints in 2024; six vexatious.
One Council member violated Code of Ethics in 2023.
Commissioner recommended posting reports online.

chips.text: Received as information
Integrity Commissioner confirmed Code of Ethics prevents "weaponization" against Council.
Members of the public filed five informal complaints in 2024.
Finding six complaints vexatious is a rare decision for integrity commissioners.
Western Integrity Commissioners committed to continuing meetings and planning a 2025 conference.

speakers.name: Angela Kruk
speakers.summary: Angela Kruk, Integrity Commissioner, was in attendance via teleconference and presented her report.
said: Presented 2024 annual report on Integrity Commissioner's functions.
Reported 14 formal complaints in 2024; 6 were vexatious.
Code of Ethics has mechanisms to prevent 'weaponization' of complaints.

description: Jory Vermette urged council to commit to net-zero emissions by 2050.
He advocated for ambitious investments in climate mitigation and adaptation.
He countered a business group's focus on cost reduction.

chips.text: Approved
Jory Vermette urged council to prioritize long-term community interests.
Speaker emphasized net-zero emissions by 2050 to avoid catastrophic climate change.
